title: Spatially Resolved AGN Ionization and Star Formation at Cosmic Noon with JWST/JEMS
comment: 26 pages, 13 figures, submitted to AAS journals
summary: At Cosmic Noon ($z\approx 2-3$), both star formation and Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) activity peaked, each playing a significant role in ionizing interstellar gas on galaxy-wide scales. The spatial distribution of this ionized gas provides a direct probe of how AGN and stellar ionization shape the gaseous reservoirs of their host galaxies. Using JWST/NIRCam imaging from the JWST Extragalactic Medium-band Survey (JEMS) we spatially map two complementary tracers of ionized gas, [O III]$+\mathrm{H}β$ and Pa$β$, in $\sim200$ galaxies at $2.5 < z < 2.9$. We apply multiwavelength AGN diagnostics to divide the sample into AGN hosts (33 galaxies), Pa$β$-detected systems (32 galaxies), and control objects (175 galaxies). We measure the [O III]$+\mathrm{H}β$ and Pa$β$ spatial extents in each population and relate them to AGN and host properties derived from Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) modeling. Both tracers exhibit systematically larger maximum radial extents in AGN hosts than in control galaxies (by $\sim0.3$ dex), with [O III]$+\mathrm{H}β$ emission modestly more extended than Pa$β$ by $\sim0.1$ dex. With this statistically robust AGN sample, we measure the [O III]$+\mathrm{H}β$ radial extent-AGN luminosity relation at $z\sim3$ and derive a slope of $\sim0.2$, consistent with the shallow end of values reported at low redshift. The larger ionized gas extents among AGN hosts relative to the control sample, combined with the strong correlation between [O III]$+\mathrm{H}β$ extent and AGN luminosity suggest that AGN activity may dominate gas ionization in galaxies with mixed AGN and star-forming activity at Cosmic Noon, although stellar processes can still contribute significantly on kiloparsec scales.

AI.tldr: JWST study maps ionized gas in ~200 galaxies at z~3, finding AGN hosts have larger ionized gas extents than control galaxies, with correlation between gas extent and AGN luminosity suggesting AGN dominate ionization at Cosmic Noon.
AI.motivation: To understand how AGN and stellar ionization shape the gaseous reservoirs of galaxies during Cosmic Noon (z≈2-3) when both star formation and AGN activity peaked, by studying the spatial distribution of ionized gas.
AI.method: Used JWST/NIRCam imaging from JEMS to spatially map [O III]+Hβ and Paβ emission in ~200 galaxies at 2.5<z<2.9. Applied multiwavelength AGN diagnostics to classify galaxies into AGN hosts (33), Paβ-detected systems (32), and control objects (175). Measured spatial extents and related them to AGN/host properties from SED modeling.
AI.result: Both tracers show systematically larger maximum radial extents in AGN hosts than control galaxies (~0.3 dex), with [O III]+Hβ modestly more extended than Paβ (~0.1 dex). Measured [O III]+Hβ radial extent-AGN luminosity relation at z~3 with slope ~0.2, consistent with shallow end of low-z values.
AI.conclusion: AGN activity may dominate gas ionization in galaxies with mixed AGN and star-forming activity at Cosmic Noon, though stellar processes still contribute significantly on kiloparsec scales, as evidenced by larger ionized gas extents in AGN hosts and correlation with AGN luminosity.

title: Constraints on the Galactic Chemical Evolution of $^3\rm{He}$
summary: We examine the galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of $^3\rm{He}$ in one-zone and multi-zone models, with particular attention to the stellar yields and GCE parameters that can reproduce both the protosolar $^3\rm{He}$ abundance and recent gas-phase $^3\rm{He}/^4\rm{He}$ measurements in the Orion nebula. Published stellar models indicate negligible net $^3\rm{He}$ production by massive stars, while the predicted yields from asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars are metallicity-dependent and span a range of $\sim 2.5$ depending on the extra mixing processes incorporated in the stellar models. The dominant contribution to $^3\rm{He}$ production comes from $1-2\ M_\odot$ stars, making $^3\rm{He}$ evolution slow compared to other AGB elements and to Fe enrichment from Type Ia supernovae. We constrain our GCE models to reproduce the observed [O/H] in the interstellar medium, and our fiducial models adopt an empirically motivated IMF-averaged oxygen yield $y_{\rm O} \approx 1.2\ Z_{\rm O, \odot}$. Even with the lowest of the AGB $^3\rm{He}$ yields, based on stellar models with rotational and thermohaline mixing, our GCE models tend to overpredict the protosolar and Orion $^3\rm{He}$ abundances; they require a slow onset of star formation and low star formation efficiency to come close to the observed values. With a higher oxygen yield, calibration to observed [O/H] implies stronger outflows, making it easier to reproduce the observed $^3\rm{He}$. Alternatively, the true $^3\rm{He}$ yield could be lower than that predicted by existing stellar models, suggesting that mixing in red giants is not yet fully captured. Future $^3\rm{He}$ measurements that probe higher metallicity environments could help distinguish these possibilities.

AI.tldr: GCE models of ³He tend to overpredict observed abundances even with lowest AGB yields; require slow star formation onset or stronger outflows to match data, suggesting possible missing mixing physics in stellar models.
AI.motivation: To understand galactic chemical evolution of ³He and reconcile discrepancies between stellar model predictions and observed abundances (protosolar and Orion nebula measurements).
AI.method: Use one-zone and multi-zone GCE models constrained by observed [O/H], incorporating metallicity-dependent AGB yields with extra mixing processes (rotational, thermohaline), and varying IMF-averaged oxygen yields and star formation parameters.
AI.result: Even with lowest AGB yields, models overpredict ³He abundances; require slow star formation onset and low efficiency or stronger outflows (with higher oxygen yield) to match observations, suggesting true yields may be lower than current stellar models predict.
AI.conclusion: Current stellar models may overestimate ³He production; missing mixing physics in red giants could explain discrepancies. Future measurements in higher metallicity environments could help distinguish between GCE parameter solutions and yield uncertainties.

title: Tree-ring structure of Galactic bar resonance in N-body simulations
summary: We study the structure and evolution of the galactic bar's resonant phase-space in self-consistent N-body simulations of the Milky Way, with and without perturbations from the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy. In an idealized disk evolution model in which stars are perturbed solely by a bar that spins down due to dynamical friction against the dark matter halo, it is predicted that stars trapped in the bar's corotation resonance form a characteristic `tree-ring' structure in phase space: as the resonance expands in volume while sweeping outwards, it sequentially captures surrounding stars at its surface, such that stars captured earlier in the inner disk are found preferentially near the core of the resonance. However, it has not been clear whether such a structure persists in a more realistic galactic disk subject to a variety of time-dependent perturbations, in particular those by spiral arms and passing satellite galaxies. This paper demonstrates that the predicted tree-ring structure indeed emerges in a realistic noisy environment using self-consistent N-body simulations. Despite the presence of spiral arms, encounters with the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy, as well as fluctuations in the bar's pattern speed, and not least numerical noise -- all of which drive stellar diffusion in phase space -- the tree-ring structure remains well-preserved in the slow angle-action space. Our results demonstrate that the tree-ring structure of the bar's resonance is a robust signal of the bar's spin-down and hence its discovery in the Milky Way implies the existence of a dark matter halo that removed angular momentum from the bar.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that the predicted 'tree-ring' structure in phase space, formed by stars trapped in the Milky Way's bar corotation resonance during bar spin-down, persists in realistic N-body simulations despite various perturbations including spiral arms and satellite galaxy encounters.
AI.motivation: Previous idealized models predicted that stars trapped in the bar's corotation resonance during spin-down should form a characteristic tree-ring structure in phase space, but it was unclear whether this structure would survive in realistic galactic environments with time-dependent perturbations from spiral arms and satellite galaxies.
AI.method: The study uses self-consistent N-body simulations of the Milky Way, both with and without perturbations from the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy. The analysis focuses on the evolution of the galactic bar's resonant phase-space structure in these realistic noisy environments.
AI.result: The predicted tree-ring structure emerges and remains well-preserved in slow angle-action space despite the presence of spiral arms, Sagittarius dwarf galaxy encounters, fluctuations in the bar's pattern speed, and numerical noise. The structure is robust against stellar diffusion in phase space.
AI.conclusion: The tree-ring structure of the bar's resonance is a robust signal of the bar's spin-down. Its discovery in the Milky Way would imply the existence of a dark matter halo that removed angular momentum from the bar through dynamical friction.

title: Low-mass Active Galaxies in the SAMI Galaxy Survey with Spatially-resolved Spectroscopy
comment: 29 pages, 20 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The smallest supermassive black holes (BHs), which provide constraints on BH seeds, reside in low-mass galaxies. Here, we present a systematic analysis of 990 low-mass galaxies in the SAMI Galaxy Survey to identify emission from accreting BHs using integral field spectroscopy (IFS). Employing a novel automated scoring algorithm based on spatially resolved narrow emission-line diagnostics, we find signatures of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in 41 galaxies, as well as an additional 46 less secure candidates. The galaxies have stellar masses in the range $10^{9.4} \lesssim M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{10}$ (down to $10^{8.5}$ including less secure candidates), redshifts $z \lesssim 0.06$, and morphologies ranging from early-type ellipticals to late-type spirals. Our AGN fraction of 4% (9% including the less secure candidates) is significantly higher than those reported by studies using single-fiber spectroscopy ($\lesssim 1$--2%). Indeed, our additional analysis of single-fiber spectra of the objects in our sample demonstrates that many of our AGN candidates detected via IFS are missed. This work highlights the advantages of IFS, particularly its ability to capture extended or off-nuclear emission from accreting BHs.

AI.tldr: Systematic IFS analysis of 990 low-mass galaxies reveals 41 AGN signatures (4% fraction), plus 46 candidates, demonstrating IFS superiority over single-fiber spectroscopy for detecting extended/off-nuclear BH accretion.
AI.motivation: To identify accreting black holes in low-mass galaxies using IFS, as these host the smallest supermassive black holes that constrain BH seed formation, and to overcome limitations of single-fiber spectroscopy which may miss extended emission.
AI.method: Analyzed 990 low-mass galaxies from SAMI Galaxy Survey using integral field spectroscopy. Employed novel automated scoring algorithm based on spatially resolved narrow emission-line diagnostics to identify AGN signatures.
AI.result: Found 41 galaxies with clear AGN signatures and 46 less secure candidates, spanning stellar masses 10^9.4-10^10 M⊙ (down to 10^8.5 M⊙ including candidates), z < 0.06, and diverse morphologies. AGN fraction of 4% (9% including candidates) significantly exceeds single-fiber studies (≤1-2%).
AI.conclusion: IFS enables more complete AGN detection in low-mass galaxies by capturing extended/off-nuclear emission, revealing higher AGN fractions than previously reported and highlighting the importance of spatially resolved spectroscopy for studying BH accretion in dwarf galaxies.

title: Euclid preparation. Non-Gaussianity of 2-pt statistics likelihood: Parameter inference with a non-Gaussian likelihood in Fourier and configuration space
summary: In this work we account for this skewness in parameter inference by modelling the likelihood through an Edgeworth expansion which involves the complete skewness tensor, composed of 1-point, 2-point, and 3-point correlators. To simplify the calculations of this expansion we perform a change of basis which reduces the precision matrix to the identity. In this basis, the off-diagonal elements of the skewness tensor are consistent with zero, while the amplitude of its diagonal match the level expected for a Gaussian underlying field. We perform parameter inference with this likelihood model and find that including only the diagonal part of the skewness is sufficient, while incorporating the full skewness tensor injects noise without improving accuracy. Despite the estimated excess skewness in the original basis, the cosmological constraints remain effectively unchanged when adopting a Gaussian likelihood or considering the more complete Edgeworth expansion, with variations in the figure of merit of cosmological parameters between the two cases below $5\%$. This result remains unchanged against variations of the survey volume and geometry, scale-cut, and 2-point statistic (power spectrum or correlation function). Using $10\, 000$ cloned \Euclid large mocks based on realistic galaxy catalogues with characteristics close to future \Euclid data, we find no detectable excess skewness on intermediate scales, due to the level of shot noise expected for the \Euclid spectroscopic sample. We conclude that the Gaussian likelihood assumption is robust for \Euclid 2-point statistics analyses in both Fourier and configuration space.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that for Euclid spectroscopic survey 2-point statistics, the Gaussian likelihood assumption is robust despite potential skewness concerns, with cosmological constraints unchanged when using Edgeworth expansion.
AI.motivation: To address concerns about non-Gaussianity in cosmological parameter inference from large-scale structure surveys, specifically whether skewness in likelihood distributions could bias constraints from Euclid 2-point statistics.
AI.method: Model likelihood through Edgeworth expansion involving complete skewness tensor (1-, 2-, 3-point correlators), simplify calculations via basis change that reduces precision matrix to identity, test with 10,000 cloned Euclid mocks based on realistic galaxy catalogs.
AI.result: Off-diagonal elements of skewness tensor consistent with zero, diagonal amplitudes match Gaussian field expectations; including only diagonal skewness sufficient, full tensor injects noise without improving accuracy; cosmological constraints unchanged between Gaussian likelihood and Edgeworth expansion (<5% variation in FoM); no detectable excess skewness on intermediate scales due to Euclid shot noise level.
AI.conclusion: Gaussian likelihood assumption is robust for Euclid 2-point statistics analyses in both Fourier (power spectrum) and configuration (correlation function) space, regardless of survey volume/geometry, scale-cuts, or specific 2-point statistic used.

title: Galaxy formation in the first billion years
comment: Based on lectures presented at the 54th Saas-Fee Advanced Course "Galaxies and Black Holes in the First Billion Years as seen by JWST", January 2025
summary: These notes present material from lectures given at the 54th Saas-Fee Advanced Course of the Swiss Society of Astrophysics and Astronomy in January 2025, entitled "Galaxies and Black Holes in the First Billion Years as seen by the JWST", and are intended for early career researchers or those new to the sub-field. My lectures covered the theory of galaxy formation with a focus on the first billion years of cosmic evolution. In these notes, I discuss cosmological structure formation, properties of dark matter halos at $z\gtrsim 6$, and whether any of the JWST observations to date present a serious and fundamental challenge for the $Λ$ Cold Dark Matter Paradigm. I then give an overview of physical processes and modeling techniques, including translating simulation-based quantities to observables, and discuss recent progress and future directions in galaxy formation modeling. The closing section presents a summary of some of the theoretical puzzles and challenges raised by the first three years of high redshift observations with JWST, and how our models of galaxy formation may need to be revised to accommodate them.

AI.tldr: Lecture notes from 2025 Saas-Fee course on JWST observations of galaxies and black holes in the first billion years, covering theory, challenges to ΛCDM, and modeling approaches.
AI.motivation: To provide early career researchers with comprehensive understanding of galaxy formation theory in the first billion years, addressing whether JWST observations challenge the ΛCDM paradigm and discussing necessary model revisions.
AI.method: Lectures covering cosmological structure formation, dark matter halo properties at z≳6, physical processes, simulation-to-observable translation techniques, and modeling approaches for high-redshift galaxy formation.
AI.result: Identifies theoretical puzzles and challenges from JWST's first three years of high-redshift observations, suggesting potential revisions needed in galaxy formation models to accommodate new data.
AI.conclusion: JWST observations present significant puzzles that may require revisions to current galaxy formation models, highlighting the need for continued theoretical development to reconcile observations with the ΛCDM paradigm.

title: Smoluchowski Coagulation Equation and the Evolution of Primordial Black Hole Clusters
summary: In arXiv:2507.07171, we demonstrate that the high-redshift supermassive black holes in the so-called "little red dots" discovered by James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) can be explained by the primordial black hole (PBH) clustering on small scales. In this paper, we present a comprehensive simulation of the successive PBH mergers within a cluster by solving the Smoluchowski coagulation equation. We derive the coagulation kernel considering both cases with and without the effects of mass segregation. Then we employ the Monte Carlo method to solve the equation, implementing the full-conditioning scheme using the discrete inverse transformation method. Our simulations determine the runaway timescales of clusters and the mass population evolution of PBHs across a wide range of cosmic redshifts, depending on the number of PBHs within the cluster and the associated density.

AI.tldr: Primordial black hole clustering explains JWST's "little red dots" as supermassive black holes via successive PBH mergers solved with Smoluchowski coagulation equation and Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.motivation: To explain the high-redshift supermassive black holes observed by JWST in "little red dots" through primordial black hole clustering and successive mergers.
AI.method: Comprehensive simulation of successive PBH mergers within clusters using Smoluchowski coagulation equation, deriving coagulation kernels with/without mass segregation effects, and solving via Monte Carlo method with full-conditioning scheme using discrete inverse transformation method.
AI.result: Simulations determine runaway timescales of clusters and mass population evolution of PBHs across wide range of cosmic redshifts, depending on PBH number within cluster and associated density.
AI.conclusion: Primordial black hole clustering provides viable explanation for JWST's high-redshift supermassive black hole observations through successive merger processes.

title: The velocity field of our Milky Way outer stellar halo based on DESI DR2
summary: Using 64,000 halo K giants from Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) second Data Release (DR2), we decompose the Milky Way (MW) stellar halo between 3 and 160 kpc into metal-rich (MR) and metal-poor (MP) components via a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The two populations are nearly equal in number but chemically and kinematically distinct: MR stars occupy highly radial orbits with velocity anisotropy of beta ~0.94 and metallicity dispersion sigma([Fe/H]) ~0.17 dex, without obvious dependence on distance, and are mainly contributed by Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus (GSE) debris. MR component dominates the inner 30 kpc and re-emerges beyond 50 kpc, implying GSE debris can extend to ~70-80 kpc. MP stars exhibit a weaker radial bias of beta ~0.46, decreasing to -0.5 beyond 80 kpc, and with a larger metallicity dispersion of sigma([Fe/H]) ~0.46 dex, showing signatures of multiple minor mergers. Both components exhibit net prograde rotation at ~10-30 kpc with a stronger azimuthal signal in the MP population. The non-equilibrium motions of the outer halo (>50 kpc) are quantified with a dipole-plus-contraction velocity field. We find that the outer halo is simultaneously contracting (~-19 km/s, distance-independent) and subject to reflex motions (increases from -19 to -44 km/s with radius), reflecting the perturbation from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). We also confirm a linear dependence of mean polar velocity for the outer stellar halo on the dipole velocity field, a direct consequence of the LMC and MW interaction. Our results provide a quantitative distance-resolved description of the MW's last major accretion event and its ongoing response to the first infall of the LMC.

AI.tldr: DESI DR2 analysis decomposes Milky Way stellar halo into metal-rich (GSE-dominated) and metal-poor (minor merger) components, revealing their distinct chemical/kinematic properties and quantifying LMC-induced perturbations in the outer halo.
AI.motivation: To quantitatively characterize the Milky Way's stellar halo structure by decomposing it into distinct populations, understand the contributions from major (GSE) and minor mergers, and measure the ongoing dynamical response to the Large Magellanic Cloud's infall.
AI.method: Used 64,000 halo K giants from DESI DR2, applied Gaussian mixture model to decompose halo into metal-rich and metal-poor components between 3-160 kpc, analyzed chemical/kinematic properties, and quantified non-equilibrium motions using dipole-plus-contraction velocity field.
AI.result: Found two nearly equal populations: metal-rich stars (beta~0.94, sigma([Fe/H])~0.17 dex) from GSE dominate inner 30 kpc and extend to 70-80 kpc; metal-poor stars (beta~0.46 decreasing to -0.5, sigma([Fe/H])~0.46 dex) show minor merger signatures. Outer halo contracts at ~-19 km/s with LMC-induced reflex motions increasing from -19 to -44 km/s with radius.
AI.conclusion: The study provides distance-resolved characterization of the Milky Way's last major accretion (GSE) and quantifies the ongoing dynamical response to LMC infall, revealing distinct chemical/kinematic signatures of different merger populations and LMC-induced perturbations throughout the outer halo.

title: Cosmological Constraints on the Generalized Uncertainty Principle from Redshift-Space Distortions
summary: We investigate the imprints of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle on cosmological scales by using redshift-space distortion measurements in combination with background cosmological data to determine constraints on the deformation parameter $β$. We consider the modified Poisson bracket related to the existence of a minimal length, which leads to a modified Raychaudhuri equation for the standard $Λ$CDM model and gives rise to a phenomenological one-parameter dynamical dark energy scenario. Through this modification, we can reveal the effects of the minimal length on the late-time structure of the universe. We employ the $f$ and $fσ_8$ measurements of the growth rate combined with background data, including cosmic chronometers, baryon acoustic oscillations and Type Ia supernova observations. The observational constraints reveal a systematically negative value for the deformation parameter $β$, with the $Λ$CDM limit lying within the 95\% credible interval. When supernova data are included, the Akaike Information Criterion indicates weak-to-strong support in favour of the GUP-modified model depending on the SNIa catalogue, while the Bayesian evidence suggests a weak preference.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates cosmological imprints of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) using redshift-space distortion data, revealing negative deformation parameter β values with ΛCDM within 95% confidence intervals.
AI.motivation: To explore the cosmological consequences of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle, particularly how the existence of a minimal length scale (predicted by quantum gravity theories) affects late-time structure formation and dark energy dynamics in the universe.
AI.method: Modified Poisson bracket formalism incorporating minimal length leads to modified Raychaudhuri equation within ΛCDM framework, creating one-parameter dynamical dark energy model. Used f and fσ₈ growth rate measurements from redshift-space distortions combined with background data: cosmic chronometers, baryon acoustic oscillations, and Type Ia supernovae.
AI.result: Observational constraints yield systematically negative values for deformation parameter β, with ΛCDM limit within 95% credible interval. Model comparison shows weak-to-strong support for GUP-modified model depending on SNIa catalog (Akaike Information Criterion), while Bayesian evidence indicates weak preference.
AI.conclusion: The Generalized Uncertainty Principle leaves detectable imprints on cosmological scales, particularly affecting late-time structure formation. The negative β values suggest specific quantum gravity signatures, though ΛCDM remains statistically compatible. The approach provides a phenomenological framework to test quantum gravity effects through cosmological observations.

title: The Galactic Halo Rotation by Weyl Incorporated Gravity
summary: A modification of the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian by introducing a coupling between the Weyl tensor and the stress-energy tensor was proposed to explain flat galactic rotation curves without the exotic (non-baryonic) dark matter (DM) [1]. The proposed coupling constant was previously determined by fitting the rotational velocities of the Milky Way and M31 modeled with constant density, yielding the same coupling constant for both [2,3]. In this work, we have modified the formalism for a variable density by modeling the galactic systems with realistic, spherically symmetric and radially varying density profiles for the baryonic matter and this analysis is applied to seven edge-on spiral galaxies of the local cluster [4-10] and the Milky Way.

AI.tldr: Modified gravity theory with Weyl tensor-stress-energy tensor coupling explains galactic rotation curves without dark matter, using realistic variable density profiles for multiple galaxies.
AI.motivation: To test a modified gravity theory that eliminates the need for exotic dark matter by explaining flat galactic rotation curves through a coupling between the Weyl tensor and stress-energy tensor, moving beyond previous constant-density models.
AI.method: Modified the formalism to incorporate realistic, spherically symmetric and radially varying density profiles for baryonic matter, applied to seven edge-on spiral galaxies from the local cluster plus the Milky Way.
AI.result: Previous work determined a coupling constant by fitting rotational velocities of Milky Way and M31 with constant density models; current work extends this to variable density profiles for multiple galaxies.
AI.conclusion: The modified gravity approach with Weyl tensor coupling provides a viable alternative to dark matter for explaining galactic rotation curves when using realistic density distributions.

title: Estimates of the Dynamic Characteristics of Binary Systems for Traversable Wormholes Search
summary: The work is devoted to the study of the possibilities of observational manifestations of traversable wormholes (WHs). The simplest binary system model consisting of a traversable WH candidate (black hole (BH), supermassive BH) and a companion star, whose motion is perturbed by a massive object (star) located on the other side of the wormhole throat, is considered. In the first case of supermassive BH as WH candidate the perturbing acceleration is analyzed and compared with a competing effect in the form of the stochastic influence of stars adjacent to the companion star. In the second case the features of the change in the radial velocity of the companion star in the model of a wide binary system with a WH are also analyzed in order to distinguish it from the following models: 1) a binary system with a BH, and 2) a triple system. For the observational accuracy in radial velocity expected in the near future, at the level of 1.5 km/s the radial velocity perturbations are detectable for all considered observation time spans. For a more realistic accuracy of 10 km/s, the spectral analysis methods become statistically significant after approximately 17 years of data accumulation. The application of spectral and non-parametric methods significantly decreases the required accumulation time compared to matched-filtering applied in isolation.

AI.tldr: Study examines observational signatures of traversable wormholes in binary systems, analyzing acceleration perturbations and radial velocity changes to distinguish wormholes from black holes or triple systems.
AI.motivation: To identify observable signatures that could distinguish traversable wormholes from other astrophysical objects like black holes or triple star systems, addressing the challenge of detecting wormholes through their gravitational effects on companion stars.
AI.method: Analyzes two binary system models: 1) supermassive black hole as wormhole candidate with companion star perturbed by object on other side of wormhole throat, comparing acceleration to stochastic stellar influences; 2) wide binary system with wormhole, analyzing radial velocity changes compared to black hole binary and triple system models using spectral and non-parametric methods.
AI.result: For 1.5 km/s radial velocity accuracy, perturbations are detectable across all observation times; for 10 km/s accuracy, spectral analysis becomes statistically significant after ~17 years of data. Spectral and non-parametric methods significantly reduce required observation time compared to matched-filtering alone.
AI.conclusion: Traversable wormholes could produce detectable observational signatures in binary systems through radial velocity perturbations, with spectral analysis methods enabling detection within reasonable observation timescales, potentially distinguishing wormholes from black holes or triple systems.

title: Diverse lifestyles of bar-like galaxies and their coevolution with the brightest galaxy in the most massive cluster of TNG50
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Clusters can provide propitious environments for bar formation in galaxies. This work studies the formation and evolution of 15 bar-like galaxies in the most massive cluster of the TNG50 simulation from the IllustrisTNG suite. The selection includes galaxies from the last simulation output from well-resolved subhalos with a strongly prolate stellar component. Eleven galaxies form or strongly enhance their bars during a pericenter passage around one or more progenitors of the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG). Two form their bars early as a result of minor mergers, one via an interaction with another massive galaxy, and one via disk instability. The bar formation times differ considerably, ranging between 3-11 Gyr. The lengths of the bars also differ, ranging between 2-6 kpc, and do not correlate with the amount of tidal forcing experienced. All galaxies have at least one pericenter passage around a BCG progenitor, but the number of interactions varies strongly and is reflected in the different amount of mass stripping the galaxies experience. Most bar formation events take place before the BCG is fully formed. In three cases, they occur just before different progenitors of the BCG merge. For six bar-like galaxies, the merger events leading to the final formation of the BCG cause significant changes of their orbits. Their diverse evolutionary histories illustrate the different paths to bar formation in clusters and emphasize the complex nature of the process, which includes coevolution with BCG progenitors.

AI.tldr: Bar formation in cluster galaxies occurs primarily during pericenter passages around BCG progenitors, with diverse formation mechanisms and timing spanning 3-11 Gyr.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation and evolution of bars in cluster galaxies, specifically examining the diverse pathways and environmental influences in the high-density cluster environment.
AI.method: Analysis of 15 bar-like galaxies from the most massive cluster in TNG50 simulation, focusing on galaxies with strongly prolate stellar components from well-resolved subhalos.
AI.result: 11/15 galaxies form/enhance bars during pericenter passages around BCG progenitors; 2 form early via minor mergers; 1 via massive galaxy interaction; 1 via disk instability. Bar lengths (2-6 kpc) don't correlate with tidal forcing. Most bar formation occurs before BCG assembly, with diverse orbital histories.
AI.conclusion: Bar formation in clusters follows multiple pathways with complex coevolution with BCG progenitors, emphasizing the importance of environmental interactions and diverse evolutionary histories in cluster environments.

title: No evidence for dynamical dark energy from the Combo correlation of GRBs
summary: Recently, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) collaboration has presented results indicating that dark energy may exhibit dynamical behavior. Calibrated gamma-ray burst (GRB) correlations can be employed to verify or reject a time-evolution of the dark energy (DE) equation of state, $ω(z)$, up to redshifts $z\sim 9$. We use the most updated catalog of GRBs fulfilling the Combo correlation and improve its calibration employing three catalogs of type Ia supernovae at redshifts $z\leq0.075$ and the Bézier interpolation of the Hubble rate, as an alternative to the cosmographic series that fails to be constraining at high redshifts. To test the evolution of $ω(z)$, we adopt a model-independent, redshift-binned DE parametrization. In both the calibration and the DE reconstruction analyses the impact of the spatial curvature on the results is explored. The calibrated Combo correlation yields a Hubble constant $H_0\sim70$ km/s/Mpc which alleviates the existing Hubble tension and is broadly consistent with current measurements, although the uncertainties prevent a high-precision measurement. Regarding the reconstruction of $ω(z)$ of DE, spatially curved scenarios are disfavored and, despite the apparent ''phantom'' behavior at $z\lesssim0.55$ due to the limited statistics caused by the shortage of nearby events, at $z>0.55$ the analysis provides statistically robust evidence in favor of the cosmological constant scenario. The Combo correlation alleviates the Hubble tension and shows no significant evidence in favor of dynamical DE. This suggests that GRBs, as distance indicators, are broadly consistent with the current cosmic distance ladder.

AI.tldr: DESI results suggest dynamical dark energy; GRB correlations test DE evolution to z~9 using calibrated Combo correlation with SN Ia data and Bézier interpolation, finding H₀~70 km/s/Mpc (alleviates Hubble tension) and no significant evidence for dynamical DE beyond cosmological constant.
AI.motivation: To test whether dark energy exhibits dynamical behavior (as suggested by DESI) using gamma-ray burst correlations calibrated with nearby supernovae, and to investigate the evolution of the dark energy equation of state up to high redshifts (z~9).
AI.method: 1. Use updated GRB catalog fulfilling Combo correlation; 2. Calibrate with three SN Ia catalogs at z≤0.075; 3. Employ Bézier interpolation of Hubble rate (alternative to cosmographic series); 4. Adopt model-independent, redshift-binned DE parametrization; 5. Explore impact of spatial curvature in both calibration and DE reconstruction.
AI.result: 1. Calibrated Combo correlation yields H₀~70 km/s/Mpc, alleviating Hubble tension; 2. Spatially curved scenarios disfavored; 3. Apparent 'phantom' behavior at z≲0.55 due to limited statistics; 4. At z>0.55, statistically robust evidence favors cosmological constant scenario; 5. No significant evidence for dynamical DE.
AI.conclusion: GRBs as distance indicators are consistent with current cosmic distance ladder. The Combo correlation alleviates Hubble tension and shows no significant evidence for dynamical dark energy, supporting the cosmological constant scenario at higher redshifts despite apparent phantom behavior at low-z due to statistical limitations.

title: Milky-Way-like stars in a galaxy core 8 billion years ago revealed by gravitational lensing
comment: The peer-reviewed version of the paper is published by Nature Astronomy, available at
summary: The assembly of stellar-dominated cores in elliptical galaxies is key to understanding how cosmic structures evolved. Gravitational lensing offers unique insights into the nature of their stars. We report the discovery of the smallest known quadruply lensed quasar (radius ~0.2"), whose lensing galaxy at redshift 1.055 (5.5 billion years after the Big Bang) features a lensing mass of only ~2x10^10 M_sun. A Bayesian analysis, based on the system's exceptional properties and standard scaling relations, allowed us to sample the central galactic initial mass function with unmatched accuracy and in a previously uncharted regime in terms of mass and redshift. We found it consistent with the Milky Way one, while excluding bottom-heavy functions. This suggests that the core either grew slowly or underwent early disruptive events altering its stellar build-up, in contrast with the classical view that bulges form rapidly and remain unchanged by later interactions.

AI.tldr: Discovery of smallest quadruply lensed quasar reveals elliptical galaxy core with Milky Way-like IMF, challenging rapid bulge formation models.
AI.motivation: To understand stellar assembly in elliptical galaxy cores and test formation scenarios using gravitational lensing to probe stellar populations at high redshift.
AI.method: Used gravitational lensing of a quadruply imaged quasar (radius ~0.2") with lens galaxy at z=1.055, combined Bayesian analysis with standard scaling relations to sample central galactic initial mass function.
AI.result: Found lensing galaxy mass ~2×10¹⁰ M☉, central IMF consistent with Milky Way type (excluding bottom-heavy functions), suggesting slow core growth or early disruptive events.
AI.conclusion: Elliptical galaxy cores may form differently than classical rapid bulge formation models, potentially through slower assembly or early disruptive events altering stellar build-up.

title: Non-minimally coupled quintessence with sign-switching interaction
summary: We propose a new non-minimally coupled quintessence model to account for the late-time dark energy dynamics indicated by recent DESI measurements. Within this framework, the quintessence density begins to decrease only when it starts to dominate the universe, which naturally accounts for the late-time onset of dark energy weakening. The coupling also induces a sign change in the effective energy transfer between dark matter and dark energy during cosmic evolution. While the scalar field itself remains canonical and never crosses the phantom divide, the modified evolution of the dark matter density gives rise to an effective crossing behavior in the observationally inferred dark energy sector. Compared with both $Λ$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM models, our model is favored more strongly by current cosmological data. This work may provide a promising avenue for understanding the observational late-time weakening of dark energy and the origin of its dynamics.

AI.tldr: A non-minimally coupled quintessence model explains DESI's observed late-time dark energy weakening through modified dark matter evolution that creates effective phantom crossing without actual scalar field crossing.
AI.motivation: To explain recent DESI measurements showing late-time weakening of dark energy dynamics, addressing the observed onset of dark energy weakening when it begins to dominate the universe.
AI.method: Proposes a new non-minimally coupled quintessence model where the coupling modifies dark matter evolution, creating effective phantom crossing behavior in observations while the scalar field remains canonical and never crosses the phantom divide.
AI.result: The model better fits current cosmological data compared to both ΛCDM and w₀wₐCDM models, with the coupling inducing sign changes in effective energy transfer between dark matter and dark energy during cosmic evolution.
AI.conclusion: Provides a promising framework for understanding the observational late-time weakening of dark energy and the origin of its dynamics through non-minimal coupling effects.

title: Consistency relations of amplitude and phase fluctuations of gravitational waves magnified by strong gravitational lensing
summary: We discuss the amplitude and phase fluctuations of gravitational waves due to wave optics lensing in the presence of both a strong lens and cosmological weak lenses. By applying the geometric optics approximation to the strong lens and treating the weak lensing potential perturbatively, we obtain the amplification factor up to the second order in the weak lensing potential. Additionally, we establish a methodology to systematically evaluate the weak lensing effects based on diagrammatic rules. Based on the derived amplification factor, we evaluate the statistics of the fluctuations and demonstrate that the consistency relations originally established in the absence of a strong lens still hold in exactly the same form when a strong lens is present. The physical origin of these relations is also discussed. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for the mean of the weak lensing signal, both the magnification of the signal and the shift of the Fresnel scale to larger scales occur, consistent with the behavior observed in the variance.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes gravitational wave amplitude and phase fluctuations from wave optics lensing with both strong and weak lenses, showing that consistency relations remain unchanged when a strong lens is present.
AI.motivation: To understand how gravitational wave signals are affected by combined strong and weak lensing effects in wave optics regime, and to determine whether established consistency relations for weak lensing alone remain valid when a strong lens is present.
AI.method: Apply geometric optics approximation to the strong lens and treat weak lensing potential perturbatively to obtain amplification factor up to second order in weak lensing potential. Develop systematic methodology using diagrammatic rules to evaluate weak lensing effects.
AI.result: Consistency relations originally established for weak lensing without a strong lens still hold in exactly the same form when a strong lens is present. Both magnification of the signal and shift of the Fresnel scale to larger scales occur for the mean weak lensing signal.
AI.conclusion: The presence of a strong lens does not alter the fundamental consistency relations for weak lensing effects on gravitational waves, and systematic diagrammatic methods can effectively analyze combined strong+weak lensing scenarios in wave optics regime.

title: SDSS J153231.80+420342.7: a triple black hole candidate with a close binary black hole
summary: We report a triple black hole candidate with a close binary black hole (BBH) in the blue quasar SDSS J153231.80+420342.7 (=SDSS J1532) at a redshift of 0.209. It shows double-peaked profiles in all narrow emission lines, which can be a signature of a dual AGN. If the double-peaked features are produced by a dual AGN, the estimated physical separation between the two cores is about 3 kpc. Alternative interpretations to the double-peaked profiles involving rotating disk-like narrow line region (NLR) and AGN-driven outflow models are also discussed for the double-peaked features. Besides, SDSS J1532 shows optical quasi-periodic oscillations (QPO) of about 0.6 yr from the ZTF and CSS light curves, with time duration longer than 14 years, which may indicate a binary black hole with about 1 mpc separation. Two alternative explanations, the disk precession and the jet precession models, are also discussed. The current results cannot completely rule out alternative models for the characteristics of spectrum and light curves. As a candidate for triple black hole with two cores in kpc scale and a close BBH in milli-pc scale in SDSS J1532, it may be going through a critical period in its evolution.

AI.tldr: Discovery of a triple black hole candidate in quasar SDSS J1532 featuring dual AGN signatures at ~3 kpc separation and optical QPOs suggesting a close binary black hole at ~1 mpc separation.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize potential multiple black hole systems in active galactic nuclei, particularly focusing on the rare case of a triple black hole system, which could provide insights into galaxy merger evolution and black hole dynamics.
AI.method: Analysis of SDSS J1532 using spectroscopic data showing double-peaked narrow emission lines for dual AGN detection, combined with photometric monitoring from ZTF and CSS revealing optical quasi-periodic oscillations to infer close binary black hole properties.
AI.result: Identified a triple black hole candidate with: 1) dual AGN signatures at ~3 kpc separation based on double-peaked narrow emission lines, and 2) optical QPOs of ~0.6 yr period lasting >14 years suggesting a close binary black hole at ~1 mpc separation. Alternative explanations (rotating NLR, outflows, disk/jet precession) cannot be completely ruled out.
AI.conclusion: SDSS J1532 represents a promising triple black hole candidate potentially undergoing critical evolutionary phase, with kpc-scale dual AGN and mpc-scale close binary black hole components, though alternative interpretations remain possible.

title: Revealing the neutrino mass through persistent homology of the cosmic web
summary: Cosmological constraints on neutrino mass offer a promising avenue for advancing our understanding of both fundamental particle physics and the evolution of cosmic large-scale structure. To overcome challenges associated with traditional probes of neutrino mass, particularly degeneracies with other parameters, we consider topological summaries of the cosmic web based on the formalism of persistent homology. We introduce persistence strips, a novel representation that segments Betti curves by topological persistence, effectively condensing two-dimensional persistence diagrams into a set of one-dimensional curves. Applied to the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations, these topological descriptors demonstrate pronounced sensitivity to neutrino mass. By constructing an emulator spanning a 10-dimensional $w_0 w_a\text{CDM} +ν$ cosmological parameter space that includes parameters degenerate with neutrino masses in conventional approaches, assuming a volume of only $(350 \, \mathrm{Mpc})^3$, we obtain neutrino mass constraints with an uncertainty of $0.05 \, \mathrm{eV}$ for the total matter field and $0.13 \, \mathrm{eV}$ for the dark matter-only field, with the strongest constraints coming from void topology. Persistence strips exhibit roughly twice the constraining power of unbinned Betti curves and, through their multi-scale, environment-dependent sensitivity, systematically break degeneracies between neutrino mass and other cosmological parameters. We pinpoint the precise physical origin of the signal, identifying two equally important contributions: sensitivity to the neutrino mass fraction, which is highest in underdense regions, and the impact of neutrinos on the distribution of dark matter. Our findings highlight the particular promise of applying topological statistics to weak lensing measurements, which directly probe the total matter distribution.

AI.tldr: Persistence strips, a novel topological representation of cosmic web structure, provide enhanced sensitivity to neutrino mass by breaking degeneracies with other cosmological parameters, achieving constraints of 0.05 eV from total matter and 0.13 eV from dark matter-only fields.
AI.motivation: Traditional cosmological probes of neutrino mass suffer from degeneracies with other parameters. The authors aim to develop more sensitive, degeneracy-breaking methods using topological analysis of cosmic structure to advance understanding of both particle physics and cosmic evolution.
AI.method: Introduce persistence strips - a novel representation that segments Betti curves by topological persistence, condensing 2D persistence diagrams into 1D curves. Apply persistent homology to FLAMINGO cosmological simulations, construct an emulator spanning 10-dimensional w₀wₐCDM+ν parameter space, and analyze both total matter and dark matter-only fields.
AI.result: Persistence strips achieve neutrino mass constraints of 0.05 eV for total matter field and 0.13 eV for dark matter-only field from only (350 Mpc)³ volume. They show roughly twice the constraining power of unbinned Betti curves and systematically break degeneracies with other parameters. Void topology provides strongest constraints, with signal originating from both neutrino mass fraction sensitivity (highest in underdense regions) and neutrino impact on dark matter distribution.
AI.conclusion: Topological statistics, particularly persistence strips, offer powerful degeneracy-breaking sensitivity to neutrino mass, with particular promise for weak lensing measurements that directly probe total matter distribution. The method identifies specific physical origins of the neutrino mass signal in cosmic web topology.
